content.text:
I submitted **index 10 (Cu 0.35 / Sb 0.65)** as the best composition. It had the highest EQE of the three I measured, at 0.0365%. All three EQE values are low, so I can't tell whether this is close to the best composition in the library.

| Index | Cu / Sb | EQE (%) | What XRD showed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 0.35 / 0.65 | **0.0365** | Almost pure CuSb2O6 (Cu:Sb = 1:2) |
| 4 | 0.57 / 0.43 | 0.0210 | Mixed phases, with extra peaks beyond CuSb2O6 |
| 13 | 0.25 / 0.75 | 0.0120 | CuSb2O6 plus an antimony oxide phase |

- **Why I started at index 10:** the stability model (MACE) puts CuSb2O6 as thermodynamically stable, and the XRD at index 10 matched it cleanly. The band-gap model (MEGNet) predicted a gap near 0 eV. I didn't hold that against it, because real CuSb2O6 absorbs well and 3.2 eV light is plenty to excite it.
- **Why index 4 second:** after the low result at index 10, I tried the copper-rich mixed-phase region. It came out lower. The band-gap model gives a small 0.5 eV gap for Cu3Sb4O12, a copper-rich phase that could be present there, which may explain the weaker result.
- **Why index 13 last:** I guessed the rising trend toward more antimony, plus a possible benefit from the second phase, would help. It gave the lowest value. I picked it over the Gaussian-process tool's first suggestion, index 7, which sits between indices 4 and 10. That region was never measured.

With only 3 measurements, the Cu 0.39–0.53 region (indices 5–9) and the most antimony-rich compositions (14–19) went unmeasured. If the best composition is in either, this result falls short of it. I used 3 of the 5 XRD scans.
